page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates comprehensive instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is paired with 32.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-range execution across compute and memory workloads, accented by strong compression metrics. Single-core stress-ng registered at 2276.39 while multi-core reached 9308.24. PassMark CPU and memory scores achieved 16760.77 and 2457.47, respectively. The instance displays exceptional throughput in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.55 GB/sec (top tier) and bzip3 decompression at 15.22 GB/sec (strong). Read memory bandwidth reached 95.73 GB/sec uncached, with write operations measured at 40.61 GB/sec. LLM text generation utilizing a small 135M parameter model ranked in the top 25% at 271.19 tokens/sec, while a 7B model achieved 10.18 tokens/sec.

The qualitative cost-efficiency profile corresponds to a balanced mid-tier general-purpose workload. Because the instance possesses no local ephemeral storage, attached remote block storage is required, shifting I/O operational dependencies to network-attached disks. The balanced 4 GB per vCPU ratio and presence of AMX and AVX-512 extensions make it well matched for enterprise web application tiers, relational database engines, microservices architectures, and lightweight machine learning inference pipelines.
